NASB.1: Now the LORD said to Abram, 'Go forth from your country, And from your relatives And from your father's house, To the land which I will show you;
NASB.2: And I will make you a great nation, And I will bless you, And make your name great; And so you shall be a blessing;
NASB.3: And I will bless those who bless you, And the one who curses you I will curse. And in you all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
NASB.4: So Abram went forth as the LORD had spoken to him; and Lot went with him. Now Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
NASB.5: Abram took Sarai his wife and Lot his nephew, and all their possessions which they had accumulated, and the persons which they had acquired in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan; thus they came to the land of Canaan.
NASB.6: Abram passed through the land as far as the site of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. Now the Canaanite [was] then in the land.
NASB.7: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, 'To your descendants I will give this land.' So he built an altar there to the LORD who had appeared to him.
NASB.8: Then he proceeded from there to the mountain on the east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and there he built an altar to the LORD and called upon the name of the LORD.
NASB.9: Abram journeyed on, continuing toward the Negev.
NASB.10: Now there was a famine in the land; so Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.
NASB.11: It came about when he came near to Egypt, that he said to Sarai his wife, 'See now, I know that you are a beautiful woman;
NASB.12: and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife'; and they will kill me, but they will let you live.
NASB.13: 'Please say that you are my sister so that it may go well with me because of you, and that I may live on account of you.'
NASB.14: It came about when Abram came into Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
NASB.15: Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
NASB.16: Therefore he treated Abram well for her sake; and gave him sheep and oxen and donkeys and male and female servants and female donkeys and camels.
NASB.17: But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
NASB.18: Then Pharaoh called Abram and said, 'What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
NASB.19: 'Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her for my wife? Now then, here is your wife, take her and go.'
NASB.20: Pharaoh commanded [his] men concerning him; and they escorted him away, with his wife and all that belonged to him.

ESV.1: Now the LORD said  to Abram, “Go from your country  and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.
ESV.2: And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
ESV.3: I will bless those who bless you, and him who dishonors you I will curse, and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”
ESV.4: So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
ESV.5: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people that they had acquired in Haran, and they set out to go to the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
ESV.6: Abram passed through the land to the place at Shechem, to the oak  of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
ESV.7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built there an altar to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
ESV.8: From there he moved to the hill country on the east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. And there he built an altar to the LORD and called upon the name of the LORD.
ESV.9: And Abram journeyed on, still going toward the Negeb.
ESV.10: Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.
ESV.11: When he was about to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance,
ESV.12: and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me, but they will let you live.
ESV.13: Say you are my sister, that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared for your sake.”
ESV.14: When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
ESV.15: And when the princes of Pharaoh saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh. And the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
ESV.16: And for her sake he dealt well with Abram; and he had sheep, oxen, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
ESV.17: But the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
ESV.18: So Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
ESV.19: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her for my wife? Now then, here is your wife; take her, and go.”
ESV.20: And Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him, and they sent him away with his wife and all that he had.

NKJV.3: I will bless those who bless you, And I will curse him who curses you; And in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”
NKJV.4: So Abram departed as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
NKJV.5: Then Abram took Sarai his wife and Lot his brother’s son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran, and they departed to go to the land of Canaan. So they came to the land of Canaan.
NKJV.6: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, as far as the terebinth tree of Moreh. And the Canaanites were then in the land.
NKJV.7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your descendants I will give this land.” And there he built an altar to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
NKJV.8: And he moved from there to the mountain east of Bethel, and he pitched his tent with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; there he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.

NKJV.10: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to dwell there, for the famine was severe in the land.

NKJV.13: Please say you are my sister, that it may be well with me for your sake, and that I may live because of you.”
NKJV.14: So it was, when Abram came into Egypt, that the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was very beautiful.
NKJV.15: The princes of Pharaoh also saw her and commended her to Pharaoh. And the woman was taken to Pharaoh’s house.
NKJV.16: He treated Abram well for her sake. He had sheep, oxen, male donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
NKJV.17: But the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

NKJV.19: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’? I might have taken her as my wife. Now therefore, here is your wife; take her and go your way.”
NKJV.20: So Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him; and they sent him away, with his wife and all that he had.

AMP.1:
Now [in Haran] the LORD had said to Abram,
"Go away from your country,
And from your relatives
And from your father's house,
To the land which I will show you;
AMP.2:
And I will make you a great nation,
And I will bless you [abundantly],
And make your name great (exalted, distinguished);
And you shall be a blessing [a source of great good to others];
AMP.3:
And I will bless (do good for, benefit) those who bless you,
And I will curse [that is, subject to My wrath and judgment] the one who curses (despises, dishonors, has contempt for) you.
And in you all the families (nations) of the earth will be blessed."
AMP.4: So Abram departed [in faithful obedience] as the LORD had directed him; and Lot [his nephew] left with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
AMP.5: Abram took Sarai his wife and Lot his nephew, and all their possessions which they had acquired, and the people (servants) which they had acquired in Haran, and they set out to go to the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
AMP.6: Abram passed through the land as far as the site of Shechem, to the [great] terebinth (oak) tree of Moreh. Now the Canaanites were in the land at that time.
AMP.7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your descendants." So Abram built an altar there to [honor] the LORD who had appeared to him.
AMP.8: Then he moved on from there to the mountain on the east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and there he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD [in worship through prayer, praise, and thanksgiving].
AMP.9: Then Abram journeyed on, continuing toward the Negev (the South country of Judah).
AMP.10: Now there was a famine in the land; and Abram went down into Egypt to live temporarily, for the famine in the land was oppressive and severe.
AMP.11: And when he was about to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, "Listen: I know that you are a beautiful woman;
AMP.12: so when the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife'; and they will kill me [to acquire you], but they will let you live.
AMP.13: Please tell them that you are my sister so that things will go well for me for your sake, and my life will be spared because of you."
AMP.14: And when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
AMP.15: Pharaoh's princes (officials) also saw her and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken [for the purpose of marriage] into Pharaoh's house (harem).
AMP.16: Therefore Pharaoh treated Abram well for her sake; he acquired sheep, oxen, male and female donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
AMP.17: But the LORD punished Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
AMP.18: Then Pharaoh called Abram and said, "What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
AMP.19: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife; take her and go!"
AMP.20: So Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him; and they escorted him on his way, with his wife and all that he had.

NLT.1: The LORD had said to Abram, “Leave your native country, your relatives, and your father’s family, and go to the land that I will show you.
NLT.2: I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make you famous, and you will be a blessing to others.
NLT.3: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who treat you with contempt. All the families on earth will be blessed through you.”
NLT.4: So Abram departed as the LORD had instructed, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
NLT.5: He took his wife, Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all his wealth — his livestock and all the people he had taken into his household at Haran — and headed for the land of Canaan. When they arrived in Canaan,
NLT.6: Abram traveled through the land as far as Shechem. There he set up camp beside the oak of Moreh. At that time, the area was inhabited by Canaanites.
NLT.7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your descendants. ” And Abram built an altar there and dedicated it to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
NLT.8: After that, Abram traveled south and set up camp in the hill country, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built another altar and dedicated it to the LORD, and he worshiped the LORD.
NLT.9: Then Abram continued traveling south by stages toward the Negev.
NLT.10: At that time a severe famine struck the land of Canaan, forcing Abram to go down to Egypt, where he lived as a foreigner.
NLT.11: As he was approaching the border of Egypt, Abram said to his wife, Sarai, “Look, you are a very beautiful woman.
NLT.12: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife. Let’s kill him; then we can have her!’
NLT.13: So please tell them you are my sister. Then they will spare my life and treat me well because of their interest in you.”
NLT.14: And sure enough, when Abram arrived in Egypt, everyone noticed Sarai’s beauty.
NLT.15: When the palace officials saw her, they sang her praises to Pharaoh, their king, and Sarai was taken into his palace.
NLT.16: Then Pharaoh gave Abram many gifts because of her — sheep, goats, cattle, male and female donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
NLT.17: But the LORD sent terrible plagues upon Pharaoh and his household because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
NLT.18: So Pharaoh summoned Abram and accused him sharply. “What have you done to me?” he demanded. “Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
NLT.19: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ and allow me to take her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and get out of here!”
NLT.20: Pharaoh ordered some of his men to escort them, and he sent Abram out of the country, along with his wife and all his possessions.

WEB.1: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
WEB.2: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
WEB.3: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who curses you. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
WEB.4: So Abram went, as Yahweh had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
WEB.5: Abram took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother’s son, all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran, and they went to go into the land of Canaan. They entered into the land of Canaan.
WEB.6: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. The Canaanites were in the land, then.
WEB.7: Yahweh appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.”  He built an altar there to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.
WEB.8: He left from there to go to the mountain on the east of Bethel and pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to Yahweh and called on Yahweh’s name.
WEB.9: Abram traveled, still going on toward the South.
WEB.10: There was a famine in the land. Abram went down into Egypt to live as a foreigner there, for the famine was severe in the land.
WEB.11: When he had come near to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “See now, I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.
WEB.12: It will happen, when the Egyptians see you, that they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ They will kill me, but they will save you alive.
WEB.13: Please say that you are my sister, that it may be well with me for your sake, and that my soul may live because of you.”
WEB.14: When Abram had come into Egypt, Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
WEB.15: The princes of Pharaoh saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
WEB.16: He dealt well with Abram for her sake. He had sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
WEB.17: Yahweh afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
WEB.18: Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this that you have done to me? Why didn’t you tell me that she was your wife?
WEB.19: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now therefore, see your wife, take her, and go your way.”
WEB.20: Pharaoh commanded men concerning him, and they escorted him away with his wife and all that he had.

and I will bless you;

and you will be a blessing.

I will bless those who bless you,

and all peoples on earth

Abram in Egypt
